svg.title: One decode step: what runs where
svg.desc: Block diagram of one decode step of Gemma 4 E4B. CPU: the tokenizer turns the prompt into token ids; the embedding lookup reads FP16 token and per-layer rows from memory-mapped tables; RoPE tables and masks are computed for the position; the 16 logit slices are concatenated and the sampler picks the next token id, which returns to the embedding lookup. Neural Engine: eight chunks run in order and pass the hidden state; chunks 0 to 6 take the embedding row, per-layer rows, RoPE tables and masks. Host-held KV cache in CPU memory: owner chunks 0 to 3 read their layers’ caches and return this step’s K/V; chunks 4 to 6 read the caches of donor layers 22 and 23. GPU: not used in the shipped path. Numbered notes give the precision, the prefill path, the scope of the placement trace, the hidden state between chunks and the KV details.

div.div: 5. Each owner chunk (0–3) reads its six layers’ caches (↑) and returns this step’s K/V (↓), which the host writes at slot p mod 512 (sliding) or p (full attention).

div.div: 6. Layers 24–41 own no KV: chunks 4–6 read the caches of donor layers 22 and 23, plus this step’s K/V of those layers from chunk 3.

div.div: All three units share one unified memory and a 6 GiB per-process limit; the Neural Engine’s copy of the weights counts against the app (about 1.3 × the size of the chunk files).
